FUNDING COMPARISON

One budget. Different funding rules.

Illustrative assumptions

Maximize modeled avoided salt application on eligible Zone A roads. Each town can select at most one equipment package.

Equipment and coverage assumptions

CAL: calibration and spreader controls. BRINE: brine / pre-wetting equipment. Prices and effects are illustrative; coverage is a uniform share of the town's eligible road sections. Fixed purchase costs do not scale with coverage.

Same capacity. Four approaches.

Town / methodRoad km coveredZone A km covered
How coverage is compared

Whole cells and partial cells

The optimum uses binary integer planning; the heuristic sorts cells by their Zone A share. Both select whole cells. Uniform coverage assumes the same fractional share on every road, while the fractional upper bound permits partial cells. These two cases are benchmarks, not executable whole-cell plans. Unused capacity is retained.

Planning limits

Capacity percentages are examples, not measured fleet capacity. Cells are not validated maintenance routes. Travel links, weather concurrency, labor, storage and safety constraints are not modeled. Coverage is independent of the equipment-budget comparison and is not a measured salt saving.

The grid uses EPSG:26986 whole-kilometer coordinates and is clipped to the town/watershed intersections. Splitting conserves road length. Approximately 78.8 m of source-record overlap remains, as in the base inventory.

November 1–March 31 in America/New_York time. ERA5's approximately 0.25° grid describes regional conditions; it does not measure road-surface temperature. Weather is context only and does not calibrate salt use or equipment benefits.

Definitions and attribution

Cold-wet hours have 2 m air temperature ≤ 2°C and preceding-hour precipitation ≥ 0.1 mm. This descriptive threshold does not diagnose road icing. Precipitation includes rain and snow water equivalent; snowfall depth is a separate variable and cannot be added to it.

ERA5 / Copernicus Climate Change Service via Open-Meteo Historical Weather API. Open-Meteo data: CC BY 4.0. Exact requests, response snapshots and checksums are included in the repository.

PROVENANCE

Data and methods.

Four official GIS layers

  • Roads
  • Towns
  • Watershed
  • Protection Zones

MWRA Wachusett Reservoir, SOURCE_ID 6000000-01S. The study includes only its intersections with the three towns, not the entire watershed.

Measurement rules

Lengths are measured in EPSG:26986. Zone A takes priority, followed by B excluding A, then C excluding A/B. Unmatched roads remain separate. Exact town-border linework is assigned once.

Investment eligibility: jurisdiction code 2, paved surface codes 3–9, excluding bicycle/pedestrian facilities. Unknown, unaccepted and state roads remain in the inventory.

Investment results estimate avoided application under assumptions, not delivered chloride loads, water concentrations or verified road-safety outcomes.
